The '''2021–22 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Iowa]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by 12th-year head coach [[Fran McCaffery]] and played its home games at [[Carver–Hawkeye Arena]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 26–10, 12–8 in [[2021–22 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fourth place. The 26 wins were the most wins in a season for Iowa since the [[Elite Eight]] team in [[1986–87 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|1986–87]] earned 30 wins. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]], [[2021–22 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]], [[2021–22 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]], and [[2021–22 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, the Hawkeyes received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and drew the No. 5 seed in the Midwest region. Despite winning 9 of its previous 10 games and boasting the second-best efficiency margin in Division 1 between February 1 and the start of the tournament, the Hawkeyes were upset by No. 12-seeded [[2021–22 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite web |title=1 team from each NCAA men's basketball tournament bracket seed line to pick — and why |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2022-03-15/1-team-each-ncaa-mens-basketball-tournament-bracket-seed-line-pick-and-why |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] |last=Wittry |first=Andy |date=March 15, 2022 |access-date=April 5, 2022}}</ref>

Sophomore forward [[Keegan Murray]] earned [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus First-team All-American]] honors, and established a new [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball statistical leaders#Scoring|school record for points in a season]]. It was the third consecutive season that an Iowa player was selected a consensus First-team All-American and set a new school record for points in a season ([[Luka Garza]], 2019–20 and 2020–21).

==Previous season==
In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Hawkeyes]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 22–9, 14–6 in [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in third place. They defeated [[2020–21 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the quarterfinal round of the [[2021 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] before losing to [[2020–21 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the semifinals. The Hawkeyes received an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the West region. They defeated [[2020–21 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Grand Canyon]] in the first round before losing to [[2020–21 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] in the second round, ending their chances at their first Sweet Sixteen since 1999. Iowa spent all but two weeks of the season ranked in the top 10 of the AP poll and ended with a No. 8 ranking.

Senior center [[Luka Garza]] was named [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]]<ref>{{cite web |title=2020–21 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309180252/https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 9, 2021 |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=July 14, 2021}}</ref> and a [[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus All-American]] for the second consecutive season. He was also named the [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|consensus National Player of the Year]] and ended his career with a [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball statistical leaders#Scoring|school-record 2,306 points]] (seventh in Big Ten history). After his last home game in a Hawkeye uniform, it was announced that his No. 55 jersey would be retired. Senior guard [[Jordan Bohannon]] ended the season with school-records of 639 assists and 364 three-point field goals (second in Big Ten history).

==Offseason==

===Returning players===
Senior guard Jordan Bohannon announced on April 26 that he would return to Iowa taking advantage of the extra year of eligibility from the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jordan Bohannon returning for another season with Iowa Hawkeyes|url=https://www.thegazette.com/sports/jordan-bohannon-returning-for-another-season-with-hawkeyes/|access-date=2021-07-14|date=2021-04-27|publisher=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|language=en}}</ref>
